data.title: Posting Cadence Clustered in a Timezone Inconsistent with the Claimed Audience
data.summary:
Converted to a candidate timezone, the cluster's posting activity concentrates inside a
single weekday working window rather than spreading across the hours a genuinely
dispersed, organic set of accounts would show, and that window does not match the
timezone the claimed personas or audience would keep.
data.description:
A real, organic audience posts at all hours, because it is made of individuals on their
own schedules. A cluster that is actually run by a small operations team posts on that
team's schedule instead — a histogram of post times, once converted to a candidate
timezone, shows a working-day shape: quiet overnight, a start in the morning, a dip
around lunch, a stop in the evening, Monday-to-Friday with the weekend off. Where that
shape appears and the local time it implies does not match the timezone the personas or
targeted audience actually keep, the cluster's operators are not where they claim to be.

The weekend and holiday calendar implied by the gaps is usually a cleaner tell than the
hourly histogram: a Friday-Saturday weekend, or a dead week that lines up with a public
holiday in one country and not the claimed one, is harder to explain away than an hour or
two of ambiguity in a working-day boundary.

The method has a real failure mode worth stating plainly: a flat or random distribution
is not evidence the cluster is organic. Shift rotas, a distributed team across several
timezones, or a scheduling tool posting at random offsets all defeat the histogram without
making the accounts any less coordinated. Absence of the pattern proves nothing; presence
of it is the finding.
data.recommendation:
* Build the histogram across the whole cluster rather than one account, and test more
  than one candidate timezone before preferring one.
* Read the weekend and holiday gaps as well as the hourly shape — a non-standard weekend
  or a mismatched national holiday is a cleaner signal than the daily window alone.
* Treat a flat or random distribution as inconclusive, not as evidence of organic origin;
  shift work and scheduling tools both defeat this method deliberately or incidentally.
* Feed the result into the attribution section as one input among others, carrying the
  same confidence caveat as the rest of that section.
data.short_recommendation: Histogram posting times against candidate timezones and weigh the result, don't lead with it alone.

disarm_techniques.tactic: TA11 — Persist in the Information Environment
